Subject: Recap: Performance SLOs + next steps for load test

Hi Alex, thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

Summary of requirements:
- Target 95th percentile latency: < 200ms for non-streaming text generate calls; for streaming token-by-token responses target tail latency < 250ms.
- Throughput target: 50 req/s sustained during steady-state; spike to 120 req/s for peak testing.
- Concurrency: ~200 concurrent sessions (clients maintaining streaming connections).
- Streaming: yes - client expects server-sent events / chunked HTTP streaming for partial tokens.
- Auth: API-key based test accounts; requests will come from FinWise-owned IP ranges.

Proposed next steps:
1) We'll provide a reference k6 script and a short load plan (ramp, steady, peak, soak).
2) You provide a 4-hour test window next week and a list of IPs to allowlist.
3) We'll create test API keys scoped to a non-prod FinWise project.
4) Rishi (cc'd) will share recommended concurrency/connection settings and any server-side headers to monitor.

I attached a first-pass load test plan and a k6 script we usually start from. If the time windows below work for you, we can lock one down:
- Tue Apr 5: 02:00-06:00 PT (preferred)
- Wed Apr 6: 22:00-02:00 PT

If you want to use Locust instead of k6 we can provide that flavor as well.

Thanks, looking forward to running this.

, Logan

Hi all, technical notes and attachments below. Summary first, then the k6 snippet and guidance.

Quick summary / checklist:
- We'll create a sandbox API key for FinWise: finwise-sandbox-20270331 (read-only generate/call scope).
- Test account: finwise-test@finwise.com (API key + password will be delivered via your secure channel).
- IP allowlist (if you need to allow callbacks from Redwood): 34.82.128.0/24, 35.196.64.0/20. If all traffic originates from your runners, no inbound allowlist is required.
- Required headers to capture: X-Request-ID, X-Trace-ID, X-Client-Version, X-Redwood-Region. We'll also emit x-redwood-model and x-rt-ms on responses for tracing.
- Streaming specifics: our server supports chunked HTTP streaming and flushes tokens as they are generated. For 200 concurrent streams we recommend a steady per-stream buffer of 4KB and a token flush interval target <= 200ms.

k6 notes (attached: k6_finwise_v1.js):
- Scenario: ramp-up 1m -> 5m to reach 50 vus (virtual users), hold 30m steady at 50 vus, then spike to 120 vus for 5m, then 15m soak at 60 vus.
- Each VU will: open streaming connection, send generate request for 1-3 prompts, keep connection open for streaming tokens until completion, then sleep 1-3s.
- Concurrency mapping: 1 VU ~= 1 concurrent stream; to simulate 200 concurrent streams run 200 VUs across distributed k6 workers.
- Metrics to capture: http_req_duration (p50/p95/p99), custom metric streaming_chunk_interval_ms, connection_open_time, token_rate_per_stream.

Locust note (if you prefer): we can provide a locustfile that spins up User classes keeping long-lived websocket or HTTP streaming connections; mapping is same (200 users -> 200 concurrent clients).

Test data / quotas:
- We've created a sandbox project that is rate-limited to the requested test profile and will not affect production. Any unexpected overload will trigger automatic circuit-breakers; we'll monitor and can pause the test.

Attachments included: k6_finwise_v1.js (k6 script), finwise-loadtest-plan-20270329.pdf (load plan with graphs).

Questions for FinWise SRE:
1) Will you run k6 from your runners, or do you want Redwood to run the script from our distributed runners?
2) Confirm the secure channel for credentials delivery (we can use your Vault or DocuSign).

, Rishi
